$comment-versioning: release-type 'simple' maintains CHANGELOG.md and the tag and edits no version file — correct here because hatch-vcs derives the version from the tag, so there is no second copy to keep in step. bump-minor-pre-major is FALSE with bump-patch-for-minor-pre-major false, so below 1.0: feat -> minor, fix and everything unlabelled -> patch, and a breaking change -> 1.0.0. Verified against release-please 17.11.1's DefaultVersioningStrategy rather than inferred: at 0.5.1, breaking -> 1.0.0, feat -> 0.6.0, fix -> 0.5.2. WHY IT CHANGED. bump-minor-pre-major used to be true, which kept a breaking change at a minor so that reaching 1.0 stayed a decision someone makes rather than one a commit message makes. The cost of that was paid by dependents: a `<1.0.0` cap was not a compatibility range, because it accepted every version this config could produce. willow-mcp tried closing it downstream with `jeles>=0.5.1,<0.6.0` and withdrew it — a tight cap also blocks this package's SECURITY patches (willow_institutional_search's SSRF defence lives in jeles/_egress.py, not in willow-mcp), and it does not catch the realistic break anyway, since an unlabelled breaking `refactor:` bumps a patch and clears any cap. So the fix belongs here: `<1.0.0` now means something, and 1.0 arrives when the code breaks compatibility rather than when someone declares it. Across 99 commits and 8 tags this package has never had a breaking change, so that trigger is rare, not hair-priced. WHAT STILL IS NOT GUARANTEED: this keys off the commit type, so it only holds when a breaking change is actually written `feat!:` or carries a BREAKING CHANGE footer. A break mislabelled as `refactor:` still ships as a patch. Dependents catch that with a contract test against the really-installed package — see willow-mcp's docs/design/fleet-versioning.md Rule 1 and its tests/test_fleet_versioning.py.
$comment-sections: Section names mirror Keep a Changelog, which willow-mcp's CHANGELOG already follows. Commit types outside this list (the fleet also uses hooks:, gate:, skills:, server:, envelopes:) are ignored for both the changelog and the version bump.
$comment-what-cuts-a-release: EVERY type listed above without "hidden": true cuts a release on its own — not just feat and fix. This comment previously claimed otherwise, and it was wrong: v0.4.1 was tagged and published to PyPI for a single ci: commit that changed a workflow file and nothing a user installs. That was survivable while releases were merged by hand, because you saw what was in them; release-please.yml now arms auto-merge, so an un-hidden type ships to PyPI unattended, and a PyPI version can never be reused.
$comment-hidden-rule: The line is: does this commit change what someone gets from `pip install willow-gate`? docs/test/ci do not — tests and workflows are not packaged, and a README edit only moves the PyPI page — so they are hidden and ride along with the next real release. build and deps stay visible because a dependency or packaging change genuinely alters the installed artifact, and hiding them would mean a dependency fix never reaching anyone, silently. refactor and perf stay visible because they change shipped code, and a version number is what you point at when a refactor turns out to have broken something. Hidden also means absent from CHANGELOG.md — release-please has no 'list it but do not release on it' setting, so this is a real trade, taken deliberately.
$comment-initial-version: initial-version 0.1.0 is read only while no release exists; release-please starts a tagless repo at 1.0.0 otherwise (learned on forge-play, whose first run opened 1.0.0 with auto-merge armed). Remove after v0.1.0 is cut.
